title: Shipped a real-time black hole sim today, AI wrote all of it. The hard part was keeping it from making a clone
author: baddie22
selftext:
I've wanted to build a black hole sim since the first real image of one was taken, and today I shipped it: Black Hole Simulator, a real-time black hole with a volumetric accretion disk you can fly around. AI wrote every line of code. I've been making games for 20 years (Strange Loop Games, we made Eco, and before that Lord of the Rings and the Dark Knight at EA and Midway), and this is the first one where my whole job was steering.

The thing I keep coming back to is clones. There's a ton of one-shot demos on X right now and most of them are clones of games that already exist, because anything you don't tell the AI, it fills in with the most predictable answer. Ask for a shooter and you get Call of Duty. The world doesn't need another Call of Duty clone.

Sid Meier's rule of thirds fits really well here: a third of a game is familiar, a third improved, a third brand new. AI can one-shot the familiar third, do the improved third with your help, and that leaves you the new third, which is the fun part anyway.

Motion is its big blind spot. A character walking straight through a table is obvious to you and completely invisible to it, and animation takes more babysitting than anything else. What helped most was giving it strict targets, like reference videos (AI generated ones work fine) so it can do a detailed analysis.

For the look of the black hole, I had the agents take a basic shader and expose hundreds of properties, then I tuned the knobs by hand over a lot of review passes until I had some really different looks out of it.

You also learn to tell when it's tied itself in knots without reading any code: every fix breaks something else, or it keeps going in circles on the same bug. Tell it to untie itself and it does a pretty good job, it just won't notice on its own.

One note since it comes up a lot here: our existing games don't use generative AI, out of respect for those audiences. On new projects we're going full boar, with an opt-out for players who aren't into it yet.

Wrote it up in more detail with GIFs: [https://johnkrajewski.substack.com/p/exploring-the-next-stage-of-game?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://johnkrajewski.substack.com/p/exploring-the-next-stage-of-game?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

It's on Steam if you want to fly around it: [https://blackholesimulator.com/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://blackholesimulator.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

Curious how others here are dealing with the clone problem, let me know what you think!
